summary: Defines the notation for ASN.1 encoding instructions that apply to the Generic String Encoding Rules, which turn ASN.1 values into readable text strings. These instructions alter how types are encoded.

plainLanguage.summary: ASN.1 describes data shapes, and GSER writes them as plain text. This note adds a way to annotate a shape so the text version is written in a particular way.

subtitle: A small notation that lets an ASN.1 CHOICE of strings be written as a bare string in GSER text.

tldr.problem: GSER writes ASN.1 values as text, and a CHOICE between string types normally needs a leading identifier. Earlier, a ChoiceOfStrings type was only declared in prose, with no machine-processable form.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 4792 defines the notation for GSER encoding instructions and one instruction, CHOICE-OF-STRINGS, with an optional PRECEDENCE list that tells a decoder which alternative to try first when the identifier is left out.
tldr.outcome: The instruction SHOULD be used instead of simply declaring a ChoiceOfStrings type, and it changes how the type is declared but not how existing GSER implementations behave. It updates RFC 3641.

today: RFC 4792 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 3641. The metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why Encoding Instructions Exist
sections.content:
Abstract Syntax Notation One (ASN.1) lets a specification annotate a type with encoding instructions, which change how values of that type are written by a named set of encoding rules. RFC 4792 defines the notation of those instructions for the Generic String Encoding Rules (GSER), the text encoding of RFC 3641.

It also defines one instruction, CHOICE-OF-STRINGS, to give a machine-processable way to declare a GSER ChoiceOfStrings type. The RFC says this instruction SHOULD be used instead of simply declaring a ChoiceOfStrings type.
sections.plainLanguage: ASN.1 describes the shape of data, and GSER writes it as text. This note adds a way to put a sticky note on a shape that says how to write it.

sections.title: Notation for GSER Encoding Instructions
sections.content:
The generic notation for type prefixes and encoding control sections comes from the ASN.1 basic notation. It includes an encoding reference that names which encoding rules are affected, and for GSER that reference is literally GSER.

The notation for a specific set of rules is left to the specification of those rules, so this document fills in the EncodingInstruction and EncodingInstructionAssignmentList placeholders. For GSER, an EncodingInstruction is a ChoiceOfStringsInstruction, and the assignment list, which only appears in an encoding control section, is empty.
sections.plainLanguage: The big rulebook leaves a blank for each encoding to fill in. This note fills in the blank for GSER, and GSER only has one kind of sticky note.

sections.title: The CHOICE-OF-STRINGS Instruction
sections.content:
The instruction lets a GSER encoder write the chosen alternative of a CHOICE of restricted string types without the leading identifier. An optional PRECEDENCE list lets the specification writer change the order in which a decoder considers the alternatives when the identifier is absent. The notation is "CHOICE-OF-STRINGS" optionally followed by PRECEDENCE and a list of identifiers.

The instruction must sit textually next to the CHOICE definition it applies to. That makes it clear to a reader that it applies to every use of the type, however the type is referenced.

Each alternative of the CHOICE MUST be a restricted string type such as PrintableString, IA5String, BMPString or UTF8String, possibly through a reference, a constraint or a prefix. Tagging is not significant. No two alternatives may have the same restricted string type, and if any alternative has a constraint, all must have exactly the same one.

Each identifier in the PrecedenceList MUST name an alternative of the CHOICE, and none may appear more than once.
sections.plainLanguage: The rules say each choice must be a different kind of text, so the reader can tell them apart. The optional list says which kind to try first.

sections.title: Effect on GSER Encodings
sections.content:
A CHOICE value is encoded with the ChoiceValue rule, which is either IdentifiedChoiceValue (an identifier, a colon and the value) or ChoiceOfStringsValue (just a StringValue). If the CHOICE is not subject to a CHOICE-OF-STRINGS instruction, the identified form MUST be used.

If the bare string form is used, a decoder MUST work out the alternative by trying the alternatives in order and accepting the first one that allows all of the characters in the string. With a PrecedenceList, the listed alternatives come first in list order, then the rest in definition order. Without one, all are tried in definition order.

An encoder MUST use the identified form whenever a decoder would pick a different alternative from the one being encoded. Otherwise it MAY use the bare string.

In the RFC's example, with PRECEDENCE basicName, a decoder checks whether the string is a valid basicName (a PrintableString) before checking extendedName (a UTF8String).
sections.plainLanguage: When the label is missing, the reader tries each kind of text in order and picks the first one that fits. If the real answer is not what the reader would guess, the writer has to include the label.

sections.title: Replacing Existing DirectoryString Declarations
sections.content:
The earlier GSER document declared the X.520 DirectoryString type as a ChoiceOfStrings type. Applications using GSER MUST now add [GSER:CHOICE-OF-STRINGS PRECEDENCE printableString uTF8String] just before the CHOICE keyword in the third and every later edition of the SelectedAttributeTypes ASN.1 module of X.520.

The second edition of X.520 has no uTF8String alternative. For compatibility, applications using GSER with that edition MUST instead add [GSER:CHOICE-OF-STRINGS PRECEDENCE printableString]. The RFC shows both resulting DirectoryString definitions.
sections.plainLanguage: There is one well-known box of this kind, called DirectoryString. This section says exactly which sticky note to put on it, with a slightly shorter note for the older version of the box.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The specification changes the manner in which ChoiceOfStrings types are declared but does not alter the existing behaviour of GSER implementations. The security considerations for GSER are unchanged and are those of RFC 3641.
sections.plainLanguage: Nothing about how the text is read or written changes, only how the rule is written down, so nothing new is risky.
